verified_subclaims: In-transaction recheck of existing target-day rows: a plan built when the target day was empty (default policy, allow_replace_existing=False) refuses with BridgeRefused when target-day rows exist at apply time; full 14-column SELECT * snapshots of target day 2026-09-22 and other day 2026-09-21 are logically identical before/after refusal.
Second application refusal: after a literal-True replace, re-applying a stale default plan refuses and the previously written rows persist unchanged.
Truthy non-boolean refusal: allow_replace_existing set to 1, "yes", and [True] each refuse with BridgeRefused; both dates' full-row snapshots unchanged in every case.
Plan lacking the "policy" key entirely refuses (plan.get("policy", {}) yields {} -> None) with both dates unchanged.
Literal boolean True authorizes replacement: deleted_replaced=1, written_rows=2, final_rows=2, other_days_unchanged=True; target day rewritten, other day 2026-09-21 unchanged.
Other dates remain unchanged across all executed cases, verified by logical row equality of the seeded other date.
